environment.description: Same application code deployed in an EKS pod. The pod spec includes a securityContext with readOnlyRootFilesystem:true and an emptyDir volume mounted at /tmp/uploads. The node runs Bottlerocket OS with SELinux in enforcing mode using the container_t context. Additionally, the pod has a Seccomp profile (RuntimeDefault) applied AND a custom Falco rule triggers alert+kill on any execve syscall where the process ancestor is python3/gunicorn and the spawned binary is NOT in [/usr/bin/exiftool, /usr/bin/convert, /bin/sh]. The cluster also runs Gatekeeper with a constraint template that mutates all pod specs to inject a sidecar that intercepts outbound network connections, but this is primarily for egress control. The key control: the Bottlerocket host has a dm-verity verified /usr partition and the container image is built with a distroless-like approach where /bin/sh is actually a restricted wrapper (provided by busybox-static compiled with CONFIG_FEATURE_SH_RESTRICTED=y) that disables command substitution, backticks, pipe operators, and semicolons in any shell invocation. The wrapper binary is bind-mounted from the host's verified partition.

config.shell_binary: /bin/sh is busybox-static with CONFIG_FEATURE_SH_RESTRICTED=y (no command substitution, no pipes, no semicolons, no backticks)
config.shell_mount: bind-mount from dm-verity verified host /opt/restricted-shell/sh -> container /bin/sh
config.falco_rule: kill on unexpected execve from python3/gunicorn parent (allowlist: exiftool, convert, sh)
config.gatekeeper_policy: egress sidecar injection for network monitoring
config.image_base: distroless-python3.11 with only exiftool and imagemagick binaries added
